title: Understanding a broken bone
overview: A fracture interrupts the continuity of a bone. This example uses the right humerus as reference anatomy.
limitation: Illustrative stages, not a prediction or treatment recommendation. The 3D model shows normal reference anatomy; injury and treatment geometry are not represented.

stages.title: Reference bone
stages.patientText: Locate the bone before discussing the injury.
stages.clinicalText: Locate the bone before discussing the injury.

stages.title: Fracture
stages.patientText: The bone has broken. The intact reference model identifies its location; it does not depict a fracture.
stages.clinicalText: The bone has broken. The intact reference model identifies its location; it does not depict a fracture.

stages.title: Assessment
stages.patientText: The clinician assesses the injury before choosing treatment.
stages.clinicalText: The clinician assesses the injury before choosing treatment.

stages.title: Support
stages.patientText: Some fractures are held in position with a cast or other support while healing.
stages.clinicalText: Some fractures are held in position with a cast or other support while healing.

stages.title: Alignment
stages.patientText: Fragments may be repositioned when surgery is appropriate.
stages.clinicalText: Fragments may be repositioned when surgery is appropriate.

stages.title: Fixation
stages.patientText: Plates, screws or rods may hold fragments in position. No device is shown in this reference model.
stages.clinicalText: Plates, screws or rods may hold fragments in position. No device is shown in this reference model.

stages.title: Healing
stages.patientText: Healing time varies with the injury and the person.
stages.clinicalText: Healing time varies with the injury and the person.

stages.title: Function
stages.patientText: Rehabilitation may help restore movement and strength. Less pain does not necessarily mean the bone is ready for normal loading.
stages.clinicalText: Rehabilitation may help restore movement and strength. Less pain does not necessarily mean the bone is ready for normal loading.

questions.prompt: Does less pain always mean a fracture is ready for normal loading?
questions.explanation: Pain can settle before the bone can tolerate normal stresses.

objectives: Explain the relationship between the reference anatomy and the scenario.
Recognize that stages are illustrative and outcomes vary.

title: Understanding tooth decay
overview: Acids produced by bacteria can damage the tooth surface. This example identifies a lower molar.
limitation: Illustrative stages, not a prediction or treatment recommendation. The 3D model shows normal reference anatomy; injury and treatment geometry are not represented.

stages.title: Surface
stages.patientText: Enamel is the outer protective surface of a tooth.
stages.clinicalText: Enamel is the outer protective surface of a tooth.

stages.title: Mineral loss
stages.patientText: Repeated acid exposure can remove minerals from enamel.
stages.clinicalText: Repeated acid exposure can remove minerals from enamel.

stages.title: Cavity
stages.patientText: Further loss can form a cavity. Progression is not inevitable.
stages.clinicalText: Further loss can form a cavity. Progression is not inevitable.

stages.title: Early intervention
stages.patientText: Early decay may be stopped or reversed with appropriate fluoride care before a cavity forms.
stages.clinicalText: Early decay may be stopped or reversed with appropriate fluoride care before a cavity forms.

stages.title: Cavity
stages.patientText: A cavity represents lost tooth structure.
stages.clinicalText: A cavity represents lost tooth structure.

stages.title: Filling
stages.patientText: A dentist may remove decayed tissue and restore the space with filling material. This model does not show a filling.
stages.clinicalText: A dentist may remove decayed tissue and restore the space with filling material. This model does not show a filling.

questions.prompt: Is early mineral loss guaranteed to become a cavity?
questions.explanation: Early decay can sometimes be stopped or reversed before a cavity forms.

objectives: Explain the relationship between the reference anatomy and the scenario.
Recognize that stages are illustrative and outcomes vary.
